intro: A confidence interval comes from one random sample, so it might miss. Build a hundred intervals from a hundred samples of the same population and count how many capture the true value. Change the confidence level and watch every interval stretch or shrink; change the sample size and watch the margin of error.
howItWorksTitle: How the intervals are built and counted
howItWorks: Each sample is drawn at random from a population whose true value is known: a proportion $p$, or a mean $\mu$ from a normal or a right skewed population. A proportion interval is $\hat{p} \pm z^* \sqrt{\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})/n}$; a mean interval is $\bar{x} \pm t^* \, s/\sqrt{n}$ with $n - 1$ degrees of freedom. An interval captures the parameter when the true value lies between its endpoints. The capture rate is counted over every interval built since the last change of sample size or population, so it settles near the level in the long run. Changing the level keeps the same samples and rebuilds their intervals.
